title: SARA South at Cerro Tololo
caption: The Milky Way and airglow above the SARA telescope, Cerro Tololo, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory, Chile
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The Milky Way rises from the horizon and stretches across the sky above Cerro Tololo in Chile, while yellow, green and red airglow seems to fill what would otherwise be a black sky.

The picture highlights one of the mountain’s roughly 40 telescopes: the SARA Cerro Tololo Telescope, run by the Southeastern Association for Research in Astronomy, a group of American universities. SARA also has telescopes in the Canary Islands and at Kitt Peak in Arizona, which give students and faculty at its member schools valuable time at the eyepiece.
Only the Chilean site can see the southern sky, though. This telescope fills that gap, letting SARA’s observers and trainees explore the whole night sky.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph credited to CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava). The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to someone standing on site.

explore: Airglow’s colors come from different atoms and molecules high in the atmosphere, such as oxygen, which can glow green or red at different heights.
alt: A very wide panorama of a mountain observatory at night, the Milky Way rising from the horizon through colorful bands of yellow, green and red airglow.
